'''''Camellia'' × ''williamsii''''' is a [[cultivar group]] of [[Hybrid (biology)#Hybrid plants|hybrid]] evergreen shrubs that are derived from a crossing of ''[[Camellia saluenensis]]'' with ''[[Camellia japonica]]''.<ref name=Rowell>{{cite book|author=Rowell, Raymond J.| title=Ornamental Flowering Shrubs in Australia| publisher=AH & AW Reed Pty Ltd|location=Australia | year=1980 | isbn=978-0589501778}}</ref> It was originally bred in 1923 at [[Caerhays Castle]] in [[Cornwall]] by [[John Charles Williams]].<ref name="Caerhays">{{cite web|title=Camellias|url=http://www.caerhays.co.uk/page.cfm?page=camellia_information|website=Caerhays Estate|accessdate=21 August 2017|archive-date=12 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190212012305/http://www.caerhays.co.uk/page.cfm?page=camellia_information|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Cultivars==
Williamsii cross camellias are hardier than most, and will grow outside anywhere in the UK. Some varieties are known to perform better in colder climates than in warmer ones. 'E.G. Waterhouse', for instance, grows better in Melbourne than it does in Sydney, where it was bred. Hybrid vigour has made the  group unusually [[floriferous]], with such varieties as 'St Ewe' flowering for four to five months (December to April in the UK).<ref name="Caerhays" /> Some crosses show the elliptical and pointed leaves of ''C. saluenensis'',<ref name="Michell">{{cite web|last1=Mitchell|first1=Bob|title=Plant of the month|url=https://www.st-andrews.ac.uk/~gdk/stabg_new/poms/2009/jan09pom.htm|website=St Andrews Botanic Garden|accessdate=22 August 2017|archive-date=10 November 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231110003550/https://www.st-andrews.ac.uk/errors/404/|url-status=live}}</ref> others the more rounded leaves of ''C. japonica''. Some crosses introduced colours new to camellias: 'Donation' is said to be Tyrian rose, 'Lady Gowrie' [[fuchsine]] pink.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Sparnon|first1=Norman|last2=Waterhouse|first2=Eben Gowrie|title=The Magic of Camellias; Creative Ideas for Japanese Flower Arrangement|date=1968|publisher=Ure Smith|location=Sydney}} Pages 36, 40.</ref> Nearly all crosses have flowers with translucent petals. 

More than 100 named cultivars have been bred.<ref name=Rowell/>

==Cultivation==

''C.'' × ''williamsii'' is an excellent companion to other [[calcifuge|acid-loving]] woodland plants such as [[rhododendron]]. It grows best in acid soil, [[soil ph|ph]]5.5-6.5, in a sunny or partially shaded, sheltered position. In areas with frost and cold winds, it should be positioned facing away from the morning sun, as the flower buds are easily damaged.<ref>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref>
